text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police are investigating possible fraud involving tender fixing, the disappearance of equipment and fake orders at transport parastatal TransNamib, possibly involving millions of dollars.

- Namibia's opposition DTA party criticised the 1997/98 budget for a lack of vision and unity of purpose. Its finance spokesman, Hans Erik Staby, said the budget had done nothing to address poverty and he doubted that projected growth rates of between four and seven percent could be achieved.
- Opposition finance spokesman Staby called for more accountability in government, saying ministers should resign if they did not meet expectations.
- The Enviroment and Tourism Ministry wants to complete the commercialisation of all state-run tourist camps before year-end. Negotiations with potential investors took place this week in Germany.
